manual.projectzomboid_prd.seasons.text: Southern hemisphere, %s days per season. Each crop only grows in its seasons.
manual.projectzomboid_prd.kitchen.text: Every meal gives an effect tied to its vegetables. Eating 4 different vegetables in a day makes you Well Nourished.
manual.projectzomboid_prd.soil.text:
Every farmland block keeps its nitrogen, organic matter and the last families harvested on it.

Fertility: every harvest uses nitrogen (corn and squash a lot). Legumes, soy and beans, put it back. On exhausted soil everything grows at 40%.

Rotation: the same family again in the same spot gives −30%; three times in a row is monoculture, −50%. Alternate, for example: tomato → beans → lettuce.

Companions: a companion within 2 blocks gives +15%, an antagonist −25%, and three different species around +10%. The three sisters, corn, beans and squash, help each other.

Compost: the compost bin gives it instead of bone meal. On farmland it adds +25 organic matter and +15 nitrogen. Spent grain from the brewery and spoiled harvest compost too.

Straw mulch: covers the soil for 4 harvests, protects it from frost down to −5 °C and adds organic matter. It shows as straw on the soil and cannot be spread twice.

The soil test kit shows all of this on any crop.
manual.projectzomboid_prd.climate.text:
Temperature depends on biome, season, height and time of day; the weather station gives a 7-day forecast and what to plant.

Greenhouse: glass roof and walls. Adds 8 °C and no frost. A heat source inside (campfire, furnace) adds more. In summer, outside snowy biomes, it needs extractors or it overheats. It does not work in deserts.

Grow room: underground, with grow lights hanging from the ceiling (1 to 5 blocks above the plants). Always 20 °C, but it needs an extractor with a vent open to the surface.

Extractors: plants evaporate water; you need one per 20 plants. They have a solar panel and regulate themselves: the fan spins when the vent is open.

Mold: at 85% humidity or more, crops go moldy and it spreads. The thermo-hygrometer in your hand shows temperature, humidity and what your setup is missing.
manual.projectzomboid_prd.processing.tex:
Drying rack: hang up to 16 of one harvest. It dries faster in dry, mild air: at 50% humidity normal speed, at 30% ×1.5 and at 90% it stops. Cold slows it down.

Rain stops it, and a full day at 85% humidity spoils the harvest. In humid climates dry it under a roof with extractors.

These dry: garlic and onion (air curing), tobacco, cannabis, coffee, chili, hops, yerba, corn, wheat (malt) and squash (gourd for mate).

Curing jar: dried tobacco, cannabis and yerba gain stars over the days (★ to ★★★). An empty-hand click shows how they are doing; sneak + click takes them out.

Quality passes on to what you make with them (joint, brownie, cigar, mate) and makes effects last up to twice as long.
manual.projectzomboid_prd.brewing.text:
Microbrewery: mash tun, brew kettle and fermenter side by side, with the kettle in the middle.

1. Mash tun: water bucket + 4 malt (dried wheat). It mashes for an hour and leaves spent grain for compost.

2. Kettle: gets the wort on its own. Add 2 dried hops and a fire below: campfire, lava, magma or a lit furnace.

3. Fermenter: gets the boiled wort; add yeast (bread + sugar). It ferments for 7 days and then fills 8 bottles.

Quality depends on the temperature where the fermenter stands: ideally 16 to 22 °C. The hydrometer shows gravity, alcohol, day and expected quality.

Mate: a squash cured on the rack becomes the gourd; with an iron nugget it is the mate. Yerba in the other hand loads it (10 servings).

With a thermos of hot water in the other hand, the mate is served again after every sip. Without the thermos it lasts once.

Fill the thermos at any water source or from a water bottle; in a furnace it comes out at 85 °C with 10 servings.
